summary: crypto-javas exfiltrates environment variables and CI secrets on install and import
details: The package advertises itself as a lightweight utility but runs a credential-harvesting flow both at install time and at import time. package.json declares postinstall: "node setup.js", which enumerates process.env and filters out only common shell variables (PATH, HOME, USER, etc.), then packages the remaining variables together with CI job metadata (GITHUB_RUN_ID, GITHUB_SHA, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, CI_JOB_ID, etc.), hostname, and local IP into a payload sent via sendToBackend() to a remote backend. index.js (the package main) additionally calls autoExecute() at top level, which constructs a SecretsHandler, reads non-shell environment variables, and POSTs them to a backend URL and API key resolved from BACKEND_URL / BACKEND_API_KEY / a.crypto-config.json file. The exclusion list is explicitly designed to preserve token- and credential-shaped variables while dropping benign shell noise, and the same exfiltration is duplicated across the install and require paths to maximize capture in CI and developer environments.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
